ledger.title: A typedef'd pointer formal subscripted in a loop and handed as pointer arithmetic keeps an unresolved-identity report its spelled `char *` twin does not
ledger.text: Registered by K4-FORMAL-CUSTODY-ALIASES. metric_escape (cmt_encode_prometheus.c:80, `cfl_sds_t description`; `switch (description[i])` in a loop and `cfl_sds_cat_safe(buf, description + i, 1)`) is blocked alone by `unknown_alias:description` in the user's 2026-11-24 current run. Reduced at base 5087f9295 (docs/reports/k4-formal-custody-aliases/scripts/probe.rs): `decl(d) = T ∧ T ≡ char * ∧ subscript(d, i) ∈ cond ∧ actual(d + i)` is Unknown, while the same body with `decl(d) = char *` is Safe, and dropping either the arithmetic actual or the subscripted loop is Safe. 1 of the 4,081 K4 leaves has a typedef'd pointer formal. DISCHARGE: locate the reader that reads the typedef'd declaration differently, desugar it as rule 62 does (C11 6.7.8p3: a typedef is the same type), with a fixture pair (typedef and spelled) and Lean parity if the reader is semantic.
